StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.issue: PowerInstanceType.Instanced (SandpitPower.cs:37). The sim's stacking check (cmds.py:308) always behaves as PowerInstanceType.None -- one shared instance per power id per owner -- so two simultaneous Sandpits on the same Insatiable would merge into one 8-count timer where C# would track two independent 4-count timers, either of which eats the player when it runs out. power_cmd gap G5 owns the mechanism and this unit is one of its 11 named ported instances; not re-verdicted (rule 3), and this power is one of the seven that "do not acknowledge the distinction at all" (unlike toric_toughness and the_bomb). DORMANT, and proven by enumerating the owner's move machine rather than asserted: LIQUIFY_GROUND_MOVE is the Insatiable's OPENING move and is never any state's follow_up (monsters/hive/the_insatiable.py:34-56 -- liquify -> thrash -> bite -> salivate -> thrash2 -> thrash, a closed loop that never re-enters liquify), so it applies Sandpit exactly once per combat. C# would also create one instance per target (TheInsatiable.cs:121-126 loops `targets`), which is one in single-player. Trigger: a second LIQUIFY, or a second player. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnStartLate.issue: SLOT and PHASE. (a) SandpitPower.cs:70-76 is AfterSideTurnStartLate with `side == CombatSide.Enemy` and NO owner/participants filter, dispatched once per enemy side; the sim uses the per-enemy on_enemy_turn_start (combat.py:301) filtered to `enemy is self.owner`. turn_structure gap G5 owns that and carries the identical verdict (rule 3) -- `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots` marks this unit PER-CREATURE:on_enemy_turn_start. (b) the `Late` phase pass does not exist in the sim at all -- hook_dispatch gap G3 / turn_structure G12 -- so this power's decrement is not guaranteed to be last among the side-start listeners. DORMANT for both: executed, `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py rosters` shows THE_INSATIABLE_BOSS is a SOLO encounter (n=1, order=['TheInsatiable']), so the per-creature slot and the side slot coincide, and the only other ported enemy-side-start listeners are owner-filtered (PoisonPower, DemonFormPower, HardenedShellPower, SlowPower, AsleepPower). Trigger: an Insatiable encounter with adds. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterRemoved.issue: The EFFECT is right and the MECHANISM is not. C#'s AfterRemoved (SandpitPower.cs:91-124) returns early on `oldOwner.IsDead || base.Target.IsDead`, hides the affected creatures, and `CreatureCmd.Kill(..., force: true)` every one that IsPlayer or is an Osty; the sim overrides `_expire` (powers.py:2610-2619) to kill `combat.player` unless `owner_gone` or the player is already dead. Two divergences. (1) SCOPE OF THE TRIGGER: `_expire` is reached from Power._tick at amount <= 0 (powers.py:74-75) and from PowerCmd.remove, but C#'s AfterRemoved is the hook for EVERY removal path including the automatic removal when the owner dies (ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath defaults true) -- which is exactly what the `oldOwner.IsDead` guard exists to neutralise, and what `owner_gone` reproduces. (2) `force: true` on the Kill has no sim analogue: the sim's CreatureCmd.kill goes through the ordinary death path, so a death-prevention listener could save the player from being eaten where C#'s forced kill cannot be prevented. DORMANT: the only ported player-side death preventer is Lizard Tail (relics/lizard_tail.py), and preventing the devour would merely leave the player at 1 HP against a 321-HP boss with no Sandpit left -- but it is a real observable difference, so it is a gap and not a deliberate-divergence. Trigger: any run holding Lizard Tail (or a future Fairy in a Bottle) into the Insatiable fight. Amount 4 matches: TheInsatiable.cs:126 applies 4m, the_insatiable.py:18 `_SANDPIT = 4`. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeSideTurnEnd.rationale: SandpitPower.cs:139-145 re-runs UpdateCreaturePositions on the enemy side end. Presentation only: the whole body is NCombatRoom / NCreature position tweening (or a NRunMusicController parameter), guarded by `TestMode.IsOn` early-returns in the source itself. Recorded rather than skipped because turn_structure gap G11 (Hook.BeforeTurnEnd(Enemy) has no sim slot) names SandpitPower as one of its eight BeforeSideTurnEnd* files -- this entry is the confirmation that for THIS power the missing slot costs nothing, because the body is a tween.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2611-2617 checks `self.owner.is_gone` before super()._expire() and `not target.is_dead` before the kill. `is_gone` is the sim's death-or-removal predicate, so it is at least as strong as IsDead. The ordering is also right: the sim snapshots owner_gone BEFORE calling super()._expire(), which is what keeps the unregister from changing the answer.
Pets/Osty belong to the other characters; the sim's `combat.player` is the whole set in Ironclad scope.
The sim kills `combat.player` unconditionally, which is the same set once pets are waived.

C# TheInsatiable.cs:127-136 creates 6 FranticEscape statuses, 3 to Draw and 3 to Discard; the_insatiable.py:65-68 adds _ESCAPE_DRAW=3 to draw and _ESCAPE_DISCARD=3 to discard. Checked here because playing one is what adds a Sandpit stack, i.e. it is the only writer of this power's amount other than the tick.
